answer: I would anchor each agent to a live operator who passes a video liveness check. First, the operator joins a call, turns on cue, and reads a phrase aloud while two reviewers match the face to an ID. Second, that check anchors the identity, and one operator is capped at three agents. Third, the network sends a new signal phrase each quarter, and a missed recheck within 48 hours suspends the agent. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 people at $40 per check: $40,000 a round, $160,000 a year. That is like counting footprints crossing a ridge, each print from a different walker.
